title: Global holiday window — ops & comms draft
content:
Context:
- We plan a company-wide holiday window (global) where most teams are on reduced capacity for the week of Dec 24–31 (example dates). This doc is a working draft for the internal announcement, FAQ, and operational runbook for SRE/Support coverage.

Primary goals:
- Be explicit about customer-facing service guarantees (what remains covered vs what is delayed).
- Minimize surprise on-call pages by setting temporary config limits and fallbacks.
- Give clear instructions for requests/exceptions (product launches, compliance items).
- Provide a single source of truth for teams and leadership.

Audience:
- All employees (primary comms + Q&A)
- Customer Success & Support teams (operational details + handoff)
- SRE & Platform engineers (oncall schedule and mitigations)
- Sales/Account teams (escalation path for enterprise customers)

Key message (short):
- Redwood will observe a constrained support window over the global holiday week: non-critical work paused, critical oncall remains staffed with augmented escalation paths. See below for how to request exceptions.

Draft subject lines (choose 1):
- "Redwood: Holiday operating cadence & support coverage (Dec 24–31)"
- "Planned holiday window — coverage, SLAs, and how to request exceptions"

Top-of-email / Slack short announcement (for internal channel):
Hi everyone — planning note: Redwood will be on a reduced operating cadence for the global holiday week (Dec 24–31).
- Non-critical requests and launches should be scheduled outside the window.
- Critical incidents will be handled through normal oncall.
- If you believe your work cannot wait and requires coverage during the holiday week, submit an exception request by Dec 10 using the form below.
More details + FAQ in Confluence: <link>
(Primary contacts: Aaron P. — ops lead, Sasha N. — support triage, Lucia C. — comms)

Slack post longer version (for #company-announcements):
Heads-up: company-wide holiday operating cadence planned for Dec 24–31.
- Why: give teams time to recharge and reduce on-call fatigue while ensuring critical systems stay online.
- What changes: reduced SLA response tiers for non-critical requests, deploy freeze for customer-impacting launches starting Dec 22, 11:59pm PT.
- Exceptions: submit requests by Dec 10: link to Jira form (OPS-4721). We'll triage.
Questions? Drop them in #ops-questions or ping @Aaron.

All-hands talking points (for leadership):
- Reason: align with company wellbeing goals and operational risk reduction during low-traffic period.
- Reassurance: we are not leaving customers unprotected — critical monitoring & incident response remain staffed, with pre-agreed escalation to leadership.
- Practical asks: label any work that must ship over the holidays and file exception. Teams should finish rollbacks and cleanup by Dec 21.

Customer-facing guidance (short note for Accounts/CS to use):
- Typical customers: no expected change; all paid enterprise customers with active SLA remain covered. For customers with custom SLAs, account teams will coordinate exceptions.
- For customers impacted by scheduled pauses (examples: non-critical batch processing, long-running migrations), notify them 2 weeks in advance and provide a plan.

Operational checklist (SRE/Platform):
- Deploy freeze: enable feature-flag to block non-emergency prod deploys starting Dec 22 23:59 PT. (Owner: platform-eng release eng).
- Paging policy: escalate pages exactly as usual; add backup rotation (cross-region) for critical pages. (Owner: oncall lead).
- Runbook updates: ensure incident runbooks for top-10 pages are up-to-date and open in the runbook viewer. (Owner: SRE docs).
- Capacity checklist: run autoscaler stress test + run backlog flush for queued jobs by Dec 18. (Owner: infra).
- Contact list: publish final oncall roster and escalation emails by Dec 15.

Oncall schedule proposal (SKETCH — needs validation):
- Normal weekday rotation continues for critical pages.
- Cross-team backup: add two extra standby engineers (one APAC, one NA) to handle overflow.
- Timeout policy: any P0 that crosses 15 min without mitigation escalates to oncall manager.

Exceptions and approvals:
- Exceptions permitted for legally required work, high-priority regulatory rollouts, and enterprise customers with contractual obligations.
- Process: file a Jira ticket with tag OPS-HOLIDAY-EX, include impact, rollback plan, and single point of contact. Exceptions reviewed weekly by the ops council (Aaron / Sasha / product PM). Deadline: Dec 10.

Anticipated Q&A (draft answers):
Q: Will customers be impacted?
A: Not for critical services. We will maintain monitoring and response for P1/P0 incidents. For scheduled non-critical work, we'll coordinate communication with customers ahead of time.

Q: Can my team ship a minor patch?
A: No routine patches. If it’s customer-blocking, file an exception with the rollback plan and oncall contact. We will fast-track if approved.

Q: How do I reach someone during the window?
A: Use the normal paging flow. For non-urgent help, open a ticket in Zendesk/Support and tag OPS-HOLIDAY. Account teams should surface urgent customer requests to @Sasha.

Q: What if there is a major incident?
A: Major incidents follow our standard incident response: page oncall, notify incident commander, escalate to leadership if threshold breached. Leadership will be notified per the incident policy.

Draft internal FAQ page notes (Confluence to publish):
- What is the exact freeze window? Dec 22 23:59 PT — Dec 31 23:59 PT (tweak dates).
- Who is exempt? List of teams + approvers (to be filled).
- How to request exception: link + sample JSON payload for Jira ticket.
- Post-holiday rollback window & debrief: first two working days in Jan reserved for stabilizations.

Action items (owners):
- Finalize dates + approval from leadership (Owner: Lucia) — by Mar 15 (placeholder).
- Publish Confluence holiday-runbook + email templates (Owner: Aaron) — by Mar 20.
- Build exception Jira template & workflow (Owner: Sasha) — by Mar 10.
- Lock release tooling for freeze (Owner: Release Eng) — by Dec 22.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Exact freeze dates (timezone treatment for APAC).
- Degree of SLA relaxation for non-enterprise tiers (legal input needed).
- Whether marketing will do a separate customer email.
- Should we provide on-call compensation/recognition for holiday shifts this cycle? (People Ops consult).

Notes to self / rough ideas: 
- Consider temporary autoscaler bump for model-serving pools during the window (lower traffic but higher risk if rollback required). Could reduce latency for small spiky traffic.
- Pre-seed extra tokens in support routing flow so triage team can operate faster.
- Add short training slot for standby engineers on Dec 19 (30 mins).

Slack/Email templates (raw) — please iterate: 
Email to staff (long):
Subject: Redwood holiday operating cadence & support coverage (Dec 24–31)
Hi team,
We’re planning a company-wide operating cadence for the holiday week (Dec 24–31). The goal is to give teams time to rest while keeping critical systems covered. Please review the full plan in Confluence (<link>).
Key points:
- Deploy freeze for customer-impacting changes starts Dec 22 at 23:59 PT.
- Critical incidents will be handled via oncall as normal; non-critical requests will be triaged with lower priority.
- Need an exception? File OPS-HOLIDAY-EX by Dec 10.
We’ll publish the final oncall roster and escalation contacts by Dec 15.
Thanks — Lucia

Draft Slack (for #ops-questions):
Planned holiday window Dec 24–31. Deploy freeze Dec 22. Exceptions due Dec 10. Ping @Aaron / @Sasha with questions.

Last check: make sure legal sign-off if we alter SLA language. Coordinate with CS on customer messaging timeline (2 weeks notice).

-- end scratchpad --
